records.title: Introduction to Accounting and Financial Reporting
records.header: ACCTG 215 Introduction to Accounting and Financial Reporting (5)
records.text: ACCTG 215 Introduction to Accounting and Financial Reporting (5) Nature and social setting of accounting; uses of accounting information; introduction of basic accounting concepts and procedures; interpretation of financial statements. May not be repeated. Maximum 15 credits allowed between ACCTG 215; ACCTG 225; T ACCT 210; T ACCT 220; and T ACCT 230 (or equivalents). Course equivalent to: B BUS 210.

records.title: Essentials of Accounting
records.header: ACCTG 219 Essentials of Accounting (4) RSN
records.text: ACCTG 219 Essentials of Accounting (4) RSN Provides an introduction to basic accounting principles and procedures; use of accounting information to make decisions from the perspective of both external investors and internal managers. Cannot be taken for credit if credit has already been earned for ACCTG 225.

records.title: Introduction to Financial and Managerial Accounting
records.header: ACCTG 220 Introduction to Financial and Managerial Accounting (5)
records.text: ACCTG 220 Introduction to Financial and Managerial Accounting (5) Emphasizes learning how to convey and understand economic concepts in accounting language and structure. Covers basic financial accounting introduction and more in-depth managerial accounting coverage (i.e., cost allocation, budgeting, and strategic performance measurement). Course overlaps with: ACCTG 225; B BUS 211; and T ACCT 230.

records.title: Fundamentals of Managerial Accounting
records.header: ACCTG 225 Fundamentals of Managerial Accounting (5)
records.text: ACCTG 225 Fundamentals of Managerial Accounting (5) Covers application of basic costing concepts and tools for planning, control, and strategic decision making. Concentrates on information useful to enterprise managers. May not be repeated. Maximum 15 credits allowed between ACCTG 215; ACCTG 225; T ACCT 210; T ACCT 220; and T ACCT 230 (or equivalents). Course equivalent to: B BUS 211. Prerequisite: ACCTG 215 and ECON 200.

records.title: Accounting and Finance Essentials
records.header: ACCTG 275 Accounting and Finance Essentials (3) RSN
records.text: ACCTG 275 Accounting and Finance Essentials (3) RSN Explores the economic foundations of accounting systems. Discusses the short-term and long-term implications of using accounting information to evaluate performance, create budgets, and analyze financial statements. Not open for credit to students pursuing a business degree.

records.title: Financial Reporting and Analysis I
records.header: ACCTG 301 Financial Reporting and Analysis I (4)
records.text: ACCTG 301 Financial Reporting and Analysis I (4) Introduces general framework for, and principles of, understanding financial reporting decisions. Students learn to apply these general principles to analyzing real world cases. Requires students to think critically about issues involving discretion and judgment. Course overlaps with: ACCTG 375; B BUS 361; and T ACCT 301. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in ACCTG 225.

records.header: ACCTG 321 Tax Effects of Business Decisions (4)
records.text: ACCTG 321 Tax Effects of Business Decisions (4) Introduces income tax structure and basic concepts of U.S. income tax law. Emphasizes practical application of tax law enabling students to understand and apply the concepts of income, deductions, credits, and tax rates of various transactions.

records.text: ACCTG 402 Financial Reporting and Analysis II (4) In-depth analysis of the reporting and valuation of various financial statement accounts. records.header: ACCTG 411 Auditing Standards and Principles (4)
records.text: ACCTG 411 Auditing Standards and Principles (4) Intensive introduction to the attest function in society today. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in ACCTG 301; and a minimum grade of 2.0 in ACCTG 320; may not be repeated.

records.title: Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis
records.header: ACCTG 440 Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis (4)
records.text: ACCTG 440 Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis (4) Uses publicly available information to analyze, interpret, and understand financial information needed to make informed decisions. Focuses on the analysis of public companies performed by external parties, with a particular focus on equity valuation. Learned tools also useful for credit analysis, predicting financial distress, and evaluating managerial performance. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in ACCTG 301; may not be repeated.
